headword: {長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}

definitions.explanation: A prolonged period away from work or school, typically lasting a week or more.

examples.japanese: {長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}を{取|と}りたい。
examples.english: I want to take a long vacation.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}に{海外旅行|かいがいりょこう}を{計画|けいかく}している。
examples.english: I'm planning a trip abroad during summer's long vacation.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{制度|せいど}では、{年|ねん}に{一度|いちど}{長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}を{申請|しんせい}することができる。
examples.english: Under the company's system, you can apply for extended leave once a year.

notes:
Refers to any vacation or leave period significantly longer than usual. In a workplace context, it often means taking a week or more off consecutively, which is uncommon in many Japanese companies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}を{取|と}る — to take a long vacation
- {長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}を{申請|しんせい}する — to apply for extended leave
- {長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}に{入|はい}る — to go on extended leave
- {長期休暇|ちょうききゅうか}{中|ちゅう} — during extended leave

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {有給休暇|ゆうきゅうきゅうか} — paid leave (specific to employment)
- {連休|れんきゅう} — consecutive holidays (usually 2–5 days around national holidays)
- {休職|きゅうしょく} — leave of absence from work (often for health or personal reasons)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Taking long vacations can be difficult in Japan due to workplace culture. Many workers feel pressure not to take extended time off ({有休|ゆうきゅう}を{取|と}りにくい). The government has promoted initiatives like "Premium Friday" to encourage more time off.
